identity: A sunlit Japanese seaside railway crossing inspired by a classic youth-basketball anime composition, with a sailor-uniform schoolgirl, teal local train, striped crossing gates, coastal road, parked cars, small station edge, and an uninterrupted blue sea horizon.
spatialComposition: The player enters from the inland south pavement, looking north toward the crossing. The waiting schoolgirl is centered just before the near rail; the train runs east-west across the right half; striped gates cut horizontally across the frame; cars and two bystanders sit left of center beyond the gate; the sea and low horizon fill every gap behind them. Behind the entry, a compact station forecourt and residential slope extend the world; east and west pedestrian routes reconnect to the coastal road after safe grade-separated rail crossings.
environment: Mostly flat constructed coastal ground with two parallel rails, asphalt streets, concrete pavements, a shallow inland rise, a narrow station platform, seawall, and broad ocean boundary. Collision geometry includes only terrain, route surfaces, rail bed, barriers, train and vehicle masses, people, station shelter, and seawall.
lighting: Clear high summer noon with strong sunlight from upper left, crisp short shadows, saturated cyan sky, bright sea, and highly readable silhouettes.
visualStyle: Polished cinematic anime-realism honoring a beloved 1990s seaside railway-crossing mood without logos or text. Paint, clothing details, reflections, rail shine, clouds, ocean texture, and foliage remain render-layer appearance rather than topology.
openingShot: Third-person composition from directly behind a centered teenage schoolgirl in a white sailor blouse, navy pleated skirt and black knee socks, standing before the lowered gate. A teal-and-cream local train crosses right-to-left on the right, two parked cars and two waiting adults occupy the left, striped barriers form strong horizontal bands, and the brilliant sea horizon spans the background.
invariants: Keep the opening viewpoint inland and south of both rails, facing north toward the sea.
Keep the schoolgirl centered from behind, fully on the safe pavement before the near rail.
Keep one teal-and-cream two-car local train as a static east-west landmark; do not imply supported vehicle behavior.
Keep lowered black-yellow crossing gates as horizontal composition lines without blocking the alternate playable pedestrian loop.
Keep the ocean horizon visible behind the crossing and avoid buildings or mountains that close it.
Keep all primary walking routes below 12 degrees and provide a continuous safe loop around the rail corridor.
Do not encode clouds, water ripples, reflections, clothing folds, painted stripes, or vegetation detail as collision geometry.
